trust_decision.summary: Decided nowhere at the pinned commit: a caller-supplied log_file_name is used verbatim as the log base name and interpolated into the Stata command `log using "<path>"` that the executor pipes to the Stata CLI, while the only defence (GuardValidator) inspects do-file *content* and never sees the name.

landing_point.why: `log_name = log_file_name or nowtime` is the parameter's only consumer; two lines later it is formatted into a filesystem path and at do.py:129 into the `log using "..."` string that is written to Stata's stdin, so this is the first place an engineer following the report lands and the exact line the published fix modifies.

fix_sites.entry_point: MCP tool `stata_do` (src/stata_mcp/mcp_servers.py:138), Python API `stata_mcp.api.stata_do` (src/stata_mcp/api/stata_do.py:33), CLI `stata-mcp tool do --log-file-name` (src/stata_mcp/cli/_parsers.py:155)
fix_sites.module_kind: core executor / Stata command builder (stata/stata_do package)

fix_sites.entry_point: same three; the new static guard `_validate_log_name` is called from execute_dofile
same three; `generate_log_command` is the public static string builder the validated name ultimately reaches
fix_sites.module_kind: core executor (public command builder, left unescaped)
core executor (comment-only change, no behaviour change)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The dofile path is already resolved and confined to the allowed roots by the `_is_within_allowed_directories` boundary check, so it is a trusted path rather than caller-controlled text; the Windows batch transport is declared untested/unsupported, and the installer/help transports are different tools from the log_file_name wrapper.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate custom log names must keep working unchanged: the default name is the `%Y%m%d%H%M%S` timestamp and the docs show names built from variables (`analysis_{dataset}`), i.e. digits, underscores and dots. An over-broad fix that allows only bare words, rejects a leading digit, requires an extension, or silently rewrites the name into something else breaks the documented default and the documented example, and also changes the path the caller is told to read back.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/stata_mcp/stata/stata_do/do.py:81 (default name), src/stata_mcp/utils/__init__.py:12 (timestamp format), docs/api/overview.md:428 (documented example)

O6_input_shapes: double quote closing the `log using "..."` literal
newline / carriage return splitting the piped Stata command script
shell metacharacters and spaces (`;`, `&`, `$`, backtick, `|`) reaching the Stata interpreter
path separators `/` and `\` and `..` segments producing a log path outside the log directory
absolute path as the log name

O8_uncovered_routes.route: dofile_path is interpolated into `do "{dofile_path}"` in the same piped command script; a quote or newline in a file name that exists under an allowed root injects further Stata commands, and the guard only validates that file's content
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The path is already resolve()d, existence-checked and confined to the allowed directories by the boundary check, so a solver reads it as trusted and outside the log_file_name advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, three lines below the fixed line

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Windows transport re-implements the same command text by hand: `log using "{log_file}"` written into a temp batch file whose name is built from `dofile_path.stem`, then run with shell=True
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix itself keeps `shell=True` with a comment saying Windows Stata requires it, and the module says Windows is not supported/tested, so the whole branch reads as out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different transport, behind an is_unix branch

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A second Stata-command implementation over a different transport: `controller.run(f"help {cmd}")` sends a caller-supplied string to a pexpect Stata session with no validation; the same cmd is also joined into cache file names
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Help is a read-only documentation lookup in another tool and another package, not the do-file log wrapper named by the advisory.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The ado installers build `ssc|github|net install {package}` from a tool argument and send it to the pexpect Stata session; the guard never inspects it (on Windows the same string is written to a do-file)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: package installation is a separate tool with its own argument surface; the advisory is about log_file_name.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: two packages away plus a second entry point in the root module

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a public `generate_log_file(log_name, extension)` that composes a path from a caller string and is not gated by the new validation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already exists as the sanctioned way to obtain a log path; a maintainer adding a log-cleanup or log-export tool would call it directly, and the published fix deliberately put the check in execute_dofile instead of here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an ado-install variant that interpolates `package` / `package_source_from` into a Stata command string
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the maintainer already writes exactly this interpolation on that line for the Windows branch; adding an SSC or net variant with a URL parameter is a small, plausible feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second, hand-written `log using "{log_file}"` builder in the Windows branch instead of reusing generate_log_command
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already contains this duplicate string construction (twice), so a maintainer fixing a Windows quoting or path bug would naturally edit it in place rather than route it through the validated helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a user-supplied name joined into a cache/project file path (`help__{cmd}.txt`) without validation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the cache-and-save feature and this join already exist; adding an export or per-project cache option is a natural extension of the same code.

O9_family: CWE-77 / CWE-78 command injection: caller-controlled string interpolated into a Stata command line (log name and do-file path), reaching the local Stata interpreter's shell escape

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling (pyproject.toml:9,28-30); deps from PyPI: mcp[cli], pandas, pexpect, psutil, pyreadstat, openpyxl, requests; console script `stata-mcp` (pyproject.toml:26); pytest dev group
O10_build.project_tests: pytest; tests/test_stata_do_boundary.py exercises the dofile boundary through a stubbed StataDo and stubbed FastMCP, tests/test_guard_validator.py exercises GuardValidator, tests/unit/test_data_info/* cover data readers. No test at the pinned commit covers log_file_name, and the fix diff adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the regex/allow-list check to `log_file_name` at the top of whichever wrapper the report names (api/stata_do.py or mcp_servers.py), or reject only the quoted-string payload, leaving the duplicate wrapper, the dofile_path interpolation and the pexpect transports open.
